Appellants by way of instant appeal claimed that all this material was brought before Adjudicating Authority at instance of one director of corporate debtor who had been removed as MD from Board after filing of application under section 7 of IBC and was not authorized - However, fact that he still appeared to be Director of corporate debtor and Adjudicating Authority had accepted material pointed out by said Director, which was found to be relevant, no interference was warranted - Further, claim of appellants denying signatures in subordination agreement was not necessary for Adjudicating Authority to decide in proceeding under section 7 - It was found that Adjudicating Authority had after considering record found that there was material in form of MOU and agreement which dealt with interest free unsecured loan and equity shares to be allotted to both parties and concluded that there was no time value of money and that it was not financial debt - Whether therefore, there were no reason to interfere with such findings recorded by Adjudicating Authority - Held, yes [Paras 7 to 9]IBC: Where Adjudicating Authority after considering record found that there was material in form of MOU and agreement which dealt with interest free unsecured loan advanced by financial creditors to corporate debtor and concluded that there was no time value of money and that it was not financial debt, findings recorded by Adjudicating Authority could not have been interfered with

I. Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether section 5(8) makes condition of interest optional by using words 'if any' as suffix to word 'interest' in main clause - Held, yes - Whether interest-free loan results into economic advantage to borrower and, hence, time value of money exists in case of interest-free loan as well and application filed under section 7 can be admitted in case of interest-free loan - Held, yes - Whether status of financial creditor as shareholder/director of company is a disqualification to file application under section 7 - Held, no [Para 7]IBC : Time value of money exists in case of interest free loan as well and same will be considered as financial debt for filing CIRP under section 7  IBC : Where loan sanctioned by financial creditor to corporate debtor was repayable after six months, limitation to file petition under section 7 would start after six months from disbursement of loan and not immediately on disbursement

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Appellant-financial creditor advanced loan of Rs. 1 crore to respondent, a real estate company for construction of a project 'Madina Heights' - Respondent assured to repay loan with interest @ 18 per cent per annum besides offering 15 per cent share in profit of project - However, respondent failed to repay loan - Appellant issued demand notice - Since payments were still not forthcoming from respondent, appellant filed a section 7 petition seeking admission of respondent into corporate insolvency resolution process which was rejected by Adjudicating Authority as non-maintainable - It was an admitted fact that there was no written contract or agreement between appellant and respondent governing terms and conditions by which sum was advanced by appellant and disbursed to account of respondent - Whether since appellant had failed to muster clinching proof and evidence in terms of financial records to show that sum advanced by them was indisputably interest-bearing and that interest had continued to accrue and was being realized as consideration for time value of money, sum advanced by appellant to respondent did not satisfy ingredients of financial debt of disbursal, time value of money and commercial effect of borrowing - Held, yes - Whether further said project was still in progress and compliances, both procedural and regulatory, were still pending and hence no occasion for default could be said to have occurred as debt was not due or payable - Held, yes - Whether thus, debt and default not having been clearly established, there was no infirmity in impugned order rejecting Section 7 application - Held, yes [Paras 21, 25, 26 and 27]IBC : Where financial creditor had failed to muster clinching proof and evidence in terms of financial records to show that sum advanced by them to corporate debtor was indisputably interest-bearing and that interest had continued to accrue and was being realized as consideration for time value of money, sum advanced by financial creditor to corporate debtor did not satisfy ingredients of financial debt of disbursal, time value of money and commercial effect of borrowing, and thus, instant section 7 petition by financial creditor was to be dismissed

Section 3(11), read with sections 3(12) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Debt - Applicant-financial creditor filed application under section 7 against corporate debtor alleging that corporate debtor, a family unit, had defaulted in repayment of a loan - Whether since as there was no loan agreement, corporate debtor had no legal obligation to repay amount due as claimed by financial creditor - Held, yes - Whether money claimed by applicant was not at all debt under section 3(11) and also there was no proof of default and, therefore, application filed under section 7 was to be rejected - Held, yes [Paras 8 and 9]IB Code: Where there was no written loan agreement money claimed by financial creditor was not debt and therefore, application filed under section 7 was to be rejected

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant-financial creditor was in management of corporate debtor which had taken a loan from SBI - Later, management of corporate debtor was transferred to 'B' - Applicant filed application under section 7 against corporate debtor alleging that corporate debtor defaulted in repaying unsecured loan taken from applicant - Whether since terms and conditions of loan agreement with SBI of which applicant was party provided that unsecured loan made available by applicant to corporate debtor did not become due for payment till bank loan was fully liquidated i.e., on 16-2-2018, application filed on 3-7-2015 claiming that corporate debtor owed an amount to applicant was pre-matured and not maintainable - Held, yes - Whether since applicant had failed to bring on record any evidence to suggest that he disbursed money against consideration for time value of money and there was no information about rate of interest on principal amount, loan did not satisfy requirement of financial debt as contemplated under section 5(8) - Held, yes - Whether thus, applicant failed to show that corporate debtor owed an amount and there was a default in payment of such debt and, therefore, application under section 7 was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 39, 40, 43, 44, 57 and 58]IB Code: Where applicant had failed to bring on record any evidence to suggest that he disbursed money against consideration for time value of money and there was no information about rate of interest on principal amount, loan did not satisfy requirement of financial debt as contemplated under section 5(8)

Section 5(8), read with sections 5(7) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Petitioners/financial creditors had advanced unsecured loans to corporate debtor under a MOU and an agreement - Even after several requests said loan amount along with interest remained unpaid, hence financial creditor filed application under section 7 - However, it was found that corporate debtor had approached canara bank for a term loan of Rs. 950 lakhs which was duly sanctioned and financial creditors as well as directors of corporate debtor had executed a subordination agreement in favour of banker, and financial creditors, together with other signatories to said agreement had undertaken that they will not sue for, collect, assign or receive payment of any claims until bank's dues are cleared - Further, loan was provided as unsecured loan and there was no interest and no time fixed to repay same - Whether therefore, unsecured loan provided by financial creditors would not fall under category of financial debt - Held, yes - Whether further, it was also evident that debt had not become due and same was not payable at this time as financial creditors were party to subordination agreement and clauses were binding on them and thus, they could not be treated as financial creditors - Held, yes - Whether thus petition under section 7 was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 15 to 18]IBC: Where financial creditors claimed to have advanced loan to corporate debtor and corporate debtor had defaulted in repayment of loan amount, since loan was provided as unsecured loan and there was no interest and no time fixed to repay same, said loan would not fall under category of financial debt

Section 5(7), read with section 7 , of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Financial creditor -  Respondent-financial creditor had given loan to appellant-corporate debtor in connection with Q-City project - Appellant had not disputed that it had taken a loan but had taken a plea that debt had become time barred - Whether since there was continuous cause of action which was evident from books of account of corporate debtor, wherein it accepted liability of loan payable to respondent-financial creditor, application under section 7 could not be held to be barred by limitation - Held, yes - Whether since disbursement was made by respondent against 'consideration for time value of money' to derive benefit of development of Q-City, respondent came within meaning of 'financial creditor' and was eligible to file an application under section 7, there being a 'debt' and 'default' on part of 'corporate debtor' - Held, yes - Whether thus, petition filed by respondent under section 7 was rightly admitted by Adjudicating Authority - Held, yes [Paras 33, 37 and 38]I  B Code: Where disbursement was made by respondent against 'consideration for time value of money' to derive benefit of development of Q-City, respondent came within meaning of 'financial creditor' and was eligible to file an application under section 7, there being a 'debt' and 'default' on part of 'corporate debtor'

Section 5(8), read with sections  7 and 60, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process - Financial debt - Appellant-financial creditor disbursed two interest bearing loans to respondent-corporate debtor - Appellant filed a summary suit before High Court for recovery of an amount with interest on ground that respondent made only part payment and a sum was due - High Court passed a decree in favour of appellant and directed respondent to pay outstanding amount along with an interest - However, due to continuous default by respondent, appellant filed an application under section 7 for initiation of CIRP against respondent - NCLT by impugned order dismissed said application on ground that amounts advanced by appellant to respondent were not financial debts as amounts advanced did not involve a time value of money - It was noted that two loan agreements clearly specified that loans were interest bearing and interest rate, time period of loans had also been specified - Whether loan agreements clearly showed that amounts advanced by appellant to respondent were in nature of financial debts, which carried time value of money - Held, yes - Whether thus, NCLT erred grossly by not considering two loan agreements and features therein were in fact relating to financial debts, which were due and payable to appellant by respondent - Held, yes [Paras 15 and 23]IBC : Where loan agreements between parties clearly showed that loans were interest bearing and were in nature of financial debts, which carried time value of money, NCLT erred in dismissing application filed by appellant-operational creditor under section 7 against respondent-corporate debtor on ground that amounts advanced were not financial debts

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant sanctioned loan facilities to respondent - On account of respondent's failure to repay debt, a demand notice was issued - Since respondent did not make any payment despite receipt of said notice, instant application was filed under section 7 - Whether in view of fact that applicant failed to produce any document to show what was agreed interest rate between parties on basis of which money was borrowed, case of applicant did not come under section 5(8)(a) and, therefore, instant application was to be dismissed -Held, yes [Paras 17 and 20]IBC : Where applicant filed application under section 7 on account of respondent's failure to make repayment of loan, since there was no document on record to show that what was agreed interest rate between parties on basis of which money was borrowed, applicant's case did not come under section 5(8)(a) and, therefore, instant application was to be dismissed

Section 5(8), read with section 238A, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Corporate debtor entered into a Development Agreement with financial creditor, in which financial creditor was required to provide a refundable Security Deposit of Rs. 12 crores, with an option to add Rs. 3 crores more - In said agreement, additional amount (up to Rs. 3.5 crores) would bear 18 percent interest, payable quarterly - However, due to non-development, financial creditor filed a section 7 application claiming financial debt and highlighted corporate debtor's default in paying interest on Rs. 3.5 crores - Corporate debtor stated that no financial debt existed and that financial creditor was a related party holding 40 per cent equity - However, NCLT admitted said application - Aggrieved by NCLT's order, appellant-suspended director of corporate debtor filed instant appeal - It was noted that letter issued by corporate debtor to financial creditor clearly indicated that advance made over and above security deposit carried interest at a rate of 18 per cent per annum, which was compoundable and payable quarterly - Whether since payment of 18 per cent interest compoundable and payable quarterly clearly indicated time value of money, said transaction would fall within ambit of financial debt under section 5(8) - Held, yes - Whether corporate debtor had acknowledged in its financial statements, amount of interest as a long-term borrowing and had referred to same as loan from financial creditor and, thus, financial creditor had been able to prove debt and default - Held, yes - Whether therefore, NCLT did not commit any error in admitting section 7 application - Held, yes [Paras 28, 29 and 30]IBC : Where letter issued by corporate debtor to a financial creditor clearly showed that an advance made beyond a security deposit by financial creditor carried interest, which was compoundable and payable quarterly and, corporate debtor had acknowledged this interest in its financial statements as a long-term borrowing, referring to it as a loan, financial creditor had proved debt and default and, therefore, NCLT did not commit any error in admitting section 7 application  IBC : Where corporate debtor had acknowledged interest in books of account on 1-4-2013 and thereafter acknowledged that interest was due in financial statements for financial years 2013 to 2018 application filed under section 7 against corporate debtor on 30-9-2019 was within limitation period

Section 5(8), read with sections 3(12) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 and rule 4 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy (Application to Adjudicating Authority) Rules, 2016 - Financial debt - Applicants claimed to be financial creditors filed instant application under section 7 on ground that respondent company had committed default in making repayment of loan of Rs. 1.20 crores, to it which included interest - In said connection, applicants filed copy of their bank account statements showing advances made by them and audited balance sheet of respondent reflecting loan amount under heading 'Unsecured Loan' - Applicants also filed their income tax returns wherein payment of TDS on interest by respondent on behalf of applicants was reflected and thus, it pointed towards fact that money was taken by respondent against consideration for time value of money - On other hand, respondent claimed that amount was advanced by applicants as contribution to capital and thus, was not a financial debt and categorization of same under head 'unsecured loan' in balance sheet would not change its nature - However, it failed to explain why amount claimed to have been taken as contribution was treated as unsecured loan - Whether thus, 'financial debt' was owed to applicants by respondents - Held, yes - Whether further, when no date had been fixed for repayment of financial debt, it would be repayable on demand and since, in instant case there had been no repayment till date, there was default in repayment of financial debt - Held, yes - Whether therefore, instant application under section 7 against respondent company was to be admitted - Held, yes [Para 17]IBC: Where claim of corporate debtor company was that amount advanced by applicant to it was capital contribution, but same was reflected in balance sheet as unsecured loan, same was to be held as 'financial debt', on default in repayment of which insolvency proceedings was to be initiated

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 and rule 3(1)(d) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy (Application to Adjudicating Authority) Rules, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether financial contract as per rule 3(1)(d) of Insolvency and Bankruptcy (Application to Adjudicating Authority) Rules, 2016 is must between corporate debtor and financial creditor for setting out terms of a financial debt including tenure of debt, interest payable and date of repayment - Held, yes - Financial creditor granted financial assistance to corporate debtor - Corporate debtor paid interest on amount disbursed by financial creditor once and thereafter, failed to pay further interest - Financial creditor filed an application under section 7 against corporate debtor - Corporate debtor resisted application on various grounds such as lack of contractual agreement and an unidentified period of loan - NCLT by impugned order admitted application under section 7 and initiated CIRP against corporate debtor - Whether financial creditor failed to establish when debt became due and payable and that corporate debtor had committed default - Held, yes - Whether since there was no agreement of loan and no document was there to stipulate period of repayment, financial creditor had failed to establish that transaction in question was a financial debt and corporate debtor had committed default - Held, yes - Whether thus, Adjudicating Authority had erroneously admitted application under section 7 and impugned order was to be set aside - Held, yes [Paras 22, 26, 27 and 33]IBC : Where financial creditor had granted financial assistance to corporate debtor but there was no agreement of loan, financial creditor had failed to establish that transaction in question was a financial debt and corporate debtor had committed default and, therefore, order of NCLT admitting application filed under section 7 by financial creditor was to be set aside

Section 5(8), read with section  7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Petitioner, a non banking financial corporation, granted financial assistance to corporate debtor - As corporate debtor failed to service interest, said loan was recalled by petitioner - Corporate debtor had neither liquidated outstanding liability nor reduced same - Instant application was filed under section 7 against corporate debtor - Corporate debtor contended that application filed by petitioner was based on contractual agreement, an undefined period of loan etc. and said financial transaction did not tantamount to financial claim - It was noted that petitioner was in business of NBFC to grant financial assistance on interest - Though it was confirmed by petitioner that no agreement was executed, however same was not mandated in cases pertaining to NBFC's - Further grant of financial assistance was evidenced by banking transaction and deduction of TDS duly deposited with Income-tax Authority and substantiated by form 26AS of petitioner - Whether insistence of corporate debtor that transaction was not a financial debt was inexplicable and defence was frivolously raised in a desperate attempt to resist initiation of CIR process - Held, yes - Whether since petitioner was entitled to seek initiation of CIR process of corporate debtor for its inability to liquidate its dues, CIRP was to be admitted - Held, yes [Para 11]IBC : Where corporate debtor failed to liquidate outstanding liability towards petitioner and contended that CIR petition was based on contractual agreement and undefined period of loan etc., since same was not mandatory in case of NBFC's, contention of corporate debtor was inexplicible and CIRP was to be admitted

Section 5(8), read with sections 5(7) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Financial debt - Applicant claimed to have disbursed a total loan of Rs. 70 lakhs to respondent out of which 40 lakh was repaid by respondent - Respondent admitted that long term loan was received and Rs. 30 lakhs was due - Whether since loan was disbursed against consideration for time value of money and said debt included both components of outstanding principal and interest, it would come within purview of financial debt and applicant could clearly be termed as financial creditor - Held, yes - Whether since corporate debtor failed to raise any good defence that a default had not occurred in repayment or that applicant's claim was not payable in law, CIRP application was to be admitted - [Paras 16 and 39]IBC : Where interest was to be paid as consideration for time value of money, that was received as long term borrowing, debt including principal and interest would fall within purview of financial debt  IBC : Pendency of any legal proceedings including company petition under sections 241 and 242 of Companies Act, 2013 cannot be an impediment or bar to initiate CIRP

Section  7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Initiation by financial creditor - Petitioner granted financial assistance to respondent-corporate debtor - In terms of agreement, loan was to be repaid after four months from date of last disbursement by petitioner and within 15 days of raising demand - Last instalment of loan was disbursed to corporate debtor on 11-11-2010 - By a notice dated 29-9-2016, petitioner requested respondent to repay loan - In view of failure of corporate debtor to repay loan, instant application for initiating insolvency resolution process was filed under section 7 on 19-4-2017 - Corporate debtor raised objection that since last disbursement was made on 11-11-2010, amount ought to have been repayable on 11-3-2001 and, thus, application filed on 19-4-2017 was time barred - Another objection was that there was an understanding between parties that petitioner’s group would acquire respondent company and, thus, loan amount was not to be repaid but was to be adjusted against acquisition cost payable by petitioner group and, in such a situation, amount infused in respondent company was in fact an investment by petitioner - Whether since demand was made by recall notice dated 29-9-2016, breach occurred or right to sue accrued when payment was not made within 15 days from date of demand and, hence, instant application was well within period of limitation - Held, yes - Whether since respondent had not produced any material to show that there was an agreement to acquire controlling interest by petitioner group, theory of acquisition could not be accepted and advance of loan amount by financial creditor could not be termed as an investment for acquiring corporate debtor - Held, yes - Whether even otherwise, since loan was an independent transaction, in absence of material supporting take over, objection raised by corporate debtor could not be accepted - Held, yes - Whether further Code nowhere provides that a certificate under Banker’s Books Evidence Act, 1891 has to be compulsorily attached with application filed under section 7 - Held, yes - Whether in view of aforesaid, instant application was to be admitted - Held, yes [Paras 5,7 and 9]CL : Where in terms of agreement, loan was to be repaid after four months from date of last disbursement by petitioner and within 15 days of raising demand and loan was disbursed in year 2010 while repayment demand was raised in year 2016, application for initiating insolvency process would not be time barred

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Appellant-financial creditor advanced loan of Rs. 1 crore to respondent, a real estate company for construction of a project 'Madina Heights' - Respondent assured to repay loan with interest @ 18 per cent per annum besides offering 15 per cent share in profit of project - However, respondent failed to repay loan - Appellant issued demand notice - Since payments were still not forthcoming from respondent, appellant filed a section 7 petition seeking admission of respondent into corporate insolvency resolution process which was rejected by Adjudicating Authority as non-maintainable - It was an admitted fact that there was no written contract or agreement between appellant and respondent governing terms and conditions by which sum was advanced by appellant and disbursed to account of respondent - Whether since appellant had failed to muster clinching proof and evidence in terms of financial records to show that sum advanced by them was indisputably interest-bearing and that interest had continued to accrue and was being realized as consideration for time value of money, sum advanced by appellant to respondent did not satisfy ingredients of financial debt of disbursal, time value of money and commercial effect of borrowing - Held, yes - Whether further said project was still in progress and compliances, both procedural and regulatory, were still pending and hence no occasion for default could be said to have occurred as debt was not due or payable - Held, yes - Whether thus, debt and default not having been clearly established, there was no infirmity in impugned order rejecting Section 7 application - Held, yes [Paras 21, 25, 26 and 27]

Section 5(8), read with  sections 5(7) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether as per section 5(8), a financial debt means a debt along with interest, if any, which is disbursed against consideration for time value of money - Held, yes - Appellant was marketing agency and respondent was TV programme/serial producer for telecast in TV channels - Respondent had share in free commercial time (FCT) in TV programs/serials - They entered into a marketing agreement whereby respondent sold rights of entire 'free commercial time' (FCT) available for programme exclusively to appellant-marketing agency for which appellant paid amount to respondent - As per said agreement appellant was to market and sell FCT - In marketing agreements and subsequent correspondence exchanged between appellant and respondent, no way it was mentioned that amount paid by appellant was to be repayable along with interest over a period of time - Whether since appellant had not disbursed money against consideration for time value of money, clam of appellant was not to be a financial debt within meaning of section 5(8) - Held, yes [Para 21]IBC: Where a marketing agency, appellant, paid amount under marketing agreement to TV programme/Serial producer in lieu of rights of 'free commercial time' (FCT), since there was no clause that amount paid by appellant was to be repayable along with interest over a period of time, same would not be give rise to financial debt

Section  5(8), read with section  7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 and section  186 of the Companies Act, 2013 -  Corporate insolvency resolution process -  Financial debt - Appellant/financial creditor advanced interest free loan to meet financial requirements of corporate debtor to discharge its liabilities towards secured financial creditors - Corporate debtor failed to repay said loan amount despite repeated demands - Financial creditor filed application under section 7 against corporate debtor - NCLT dismissed said application on ground that amount given by the appellant to the corporate debtor was not a financial debt and that loan was given in violation of section 186 of Companies Act, 2013 and, thus, was void - It was noted that amount in question was continuously reflected in balance sheet of corporate debtor as unsecured loan without any caveat, and, therefore, such entry without any qualification/caveat was acknowledgment of debt by corporate debtor as unsecured loan having commercial effect of borrowing - Whether corporate debtor could not take shelter of section 186 of Companies Act to deny its liability to return amount taken by it being a corporate body, which was due and payable - Held, yes - Whether since financial creditor had already proved on record about amount which was disbursed as it had not been disputed and that said amount was debt fully reflected in its balance sheet continuously as an unsecured loan and had not been paid despite fact that repeated demands were made, it fell within definition of default on part of corporate debtor and, therefore, NCLT had committed a patent error in dismissing application filed under section 7 - Held, yes [Paras 20, 22, 25 and 26]

Section 5(8), read with sections 5(7) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Appellant entered into Letter of Intent (LoI) for disbursing advance for marketing/financial requirements of development project to be undertaken by respondent corporate debtor - Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was also enclosed containing terms and conditions and manner of advance to be made by appellant for development of property of corporate debtor - In pursuance of said letter, appellant had advanced different amounts to corporate debtor totalling Rs. 41.75 crores - Corporate debtor sent a letter denying signing and executing MoU - It was also alleged that appellant had failed to raise required funds as promised - Appellant filed a Commercial Suit for recovery wherein an interim injunction order was issued expressing opinion that there was a clear admission of liability - Thereafter, an application was filed under section 7 by appellant claiming as financial creditor for recovery of amount of Rs. 41.75 crores together with interest accrued thereon at rate of 18 per cent - Adjudicating Authority rejected application filed under section 7, holding that arrangement between parties was in nature of business sharing and there was no 'financial debt' - However, on consideration of documents and correspondences, including balance sheets, it was evident that amount paid to corporate debtor as advance for marketing/financial requirements of development project undertaken by corporate debtor was nothing but a financial debt within meaning of IBC - Whether therefore, Adjudicating Authority committed error in holding that appellant was not a financial creditor and rejecting application filed by appellant under section 7 - Held, yes [Paras 19, 21 and 25]IBC : Where on consideration of documents and correspondences, including balance sheets, it was evident that amount paid to corporate debtor as advance for marketing/financial requirements of development project undertaken by corporate debtor was nothing but a financial debt, Adjudicating Authority committed error in holding that appellant was not a 'financial creditor'  IBC : There being acknowledgement of debt in balance sheet, there shall be fresh period of limitation on each acknowledgement, thereby, attracting provisions of section 18 of limitation Act, 1963

Section 5(8), read with section 238A, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Corporate debtor entered into a Development Agreement with financial creditor, in which financial creditor was required to provide a refundable Security Deposit of Rs. 12 crores, with an option to add Rs. 3 crores more - In said agreement, additional amount (up to Rs. 3.5 crores) would bear 18 percent interest, payable quarterly - However, due to non-development, financial creditor filed a section 7 application claiming financial debt and highlighted corporate debtor's default in paying interest on Rs. 3.5 crores - Corporate debtor stated that no financial debt existed and that financial creditor was a related party holding 40 per cent equity - However, NCLT admitted said application - Aggrieved by NCLT's order, appellant-suspended director of corporate debtor filed instant appeal - It was noted that letter issued by corporate debtor to financial creditor clearly indicated that advance made over and above security deposit carried interest at a rate of 18 per cent per annum, which was compoundable and payable quarterly - Whether since payment of 18 per cent interest compoundable and payable quarterly clearly indicated time value of money, said transaction would fall within ambit of financial debt under section 5(8) - Held, yes - Whether corporate debtor had acknowledged in its financial statements, amount of interest as a long-term borrowing and had referred to same as loan from financial creditor and, thus, financial creditor had been able to prove debt and default - Held, yes - Whether therefore, NCLT did not commit any error in admitting section 7 application - Held, yes [Paras 28, 29 and 30]  Section 238A of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Limitation period - Whether where corporate debtor had acknowledged, interest in books of account on 1-4-2013 and thereafter acknowledged that interest was due in financial statements for financial years 2013 to 2018, application filed on 30-9-2019 was within limitation period - Held, yes [Para 28]

Section 238A, read with section 5(8), of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 and Section 186 of Companies Act, 2013 - Limitation period - Corporate debtor had availed loan from financial creditor and mortgaged its immovable property - Since corporate debtor had defaulted in making repayment, financial creditor filed an application under section 7 - Corporate debtor raised a dispute that said section 7 application was time barred; loan transaction was in violation of Section 186 of Companies Act 2013 - It was evident from loan agreement and account statement of financial creditor that loan amount was disbursed on 07.5.2015 - Loan amount had been acknowledged by Corporate Debtor in its Balance Sheet for financial year 2017-18, 2018-19, 2021-22 and 2022-2023 - Thus, it was crystal clear that section 7 application filed on 30.03.2024 was within limitation period of three years - Further, financial creditor could grant loan to extent of 60% of its paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium account loan without any resolution being passed at general meeting - In instant case, loan amount of Rs. 2.50 crore was provided in year 2015; however, from balance sheet of Financial Creditor, it was evident that in year 2015, paid-up capital of Financial Creditor was Rs.66.42 lakh with Reserve and Surplus amounting to Rs. 124 Crores - Thus, in year 2015, total shareholders fund were amounting to Rs. 125 Crores, which was within limits as provided by clause (c) of Sub Section 2 of Section 186 of Companies Act 2013 - Further, default in repayment of financial debt was not refuted by Corporate Debtor -Whether in view of aforesaid, instant application was to be admitted - Held, yes [Paras 24, 37, 41, 42, 44 and 46]

Section 5(8), read with sections 5(6) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Financial Creditor's/applicants provided loan facilities to corporate debtor - Corporate debtor committed default in repayment - Thus, applicants filed instant petition under section 7 - In instant petition, corporate debtor alleged that neither any loan was taken, nor payment of interest was payable by corporate debtor to applicants - Whether onus lies on applicants to establish that loan was given against consideration for time value of money and debt claimed comes within purview of financial debt - Held, yes - Whether since applicants had failed to bring on record any evidence to suggest that they had disbursed money to corporate debtor against consideration for time value of money, loan given by applicants would not come within purview of financial debt and applicants could not be treated as financial creditors - Held, yes [Paras 29, 30, 31 and 32]IBC: Where applicants claiming to be financial creditors, failed to prove that they had disbursed money to corporate debtor, against consideration for time value of money, loan, if any, given would not come within purview of financial debt and, thus, applicants were not financial creditors

Section 5(8), read with  section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant sanctioned various loan facilities to respondent - On account of failure of respondent to repay loan as per agreed terms, a notice was issued under section 8 - Respondent did not send any reply to said notice - Applicant thus filed instant application under section 7 - It was undisputed that respondent had taken credit facilities against payment of interest as agreed between parties - Thus, loan was disbursed against consideration of time value of money with a clear commercial effect of borrowing - Whether in view of aforesaid it could be concluded that claim raised by applicant would come within purview of 'financial debt' and applicant bank could be termed as 'financial creditor' - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, when applicant had placed on record voluminous and overwhelming evidence in support of claim as well as default in payment of financial debt, instant application deserved to be admitted - Held, yes [Paras 36 and 42]IB Code : Where applicant sanctioned various loan facilities to respondent on interest basis, in view of failure of respondent to repay said loan alongwith interest, instant application filed under section 7 was to be admitted

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant advanced Rs. 2.5 crores to respondent under a draft MoU for development of a project - An amount of Rs. 1.5 crore was admittedly returned - MoUs proposed between applicant and R1 were only draft documents and there was no document or agreement which showed terms on which money was given, nor did it specifically showed whether any interest or consideration against time value for money was payable - Further, there was no repayment schedule - Whether advance paid by applicant to R1 would have no commercial effect of borrowing and same was not financial debt - Held, yes - Whether, thus, CIRP petition was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Para 7]IBC: Where advance was paid and there was no document or agreement which showed terms of payment of any interest or consideration against time value for money, same was not a financial debt

Section 3(11), read with  section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Debt - Case of applicant/financial creditor was that she had granted unsecured loan to respondent/corporate debtor - According to applicant, since respondent failed to repay amount of loan along with interest as per terms of agreement, it was constrained to file instant application under section 7 - It was noted from record that on date of filing of application, entire term loan was not fully liquidated and all loans, provided by unsecured creditors to respondent, did not become due for payment - It was also found from loan agreements that loan given by applicant to corporate debtor was non-interest bearing one - However, applicant not only demanded repayment of principal amounts and that too well before such loan became due but also claimed interest - Whether such demand was impermissible demand - Held, yes - Whether in view of fact that on date of filing instant application, debt due to applicant had not fallen due for payment and, moreover, quantum of debt also suffered from ambiguity, imprecision and vagueness, application so filed deserved to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 58, 59 and 75]

Section 5(8), read with sections  7 and 60, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process - Financial debt - Appellant-financial creditor disbursed two interest bearing loans to respondent-corporate debtor - Appellant filed a summary suit before High Court for recovery of an amount with interest on ground that respondent made only part payment and a sum was due - High Court passed a decree in favour of appellant and directed respondent to pay outstanding amount along with an interest - However, due to continuous default by respondent, appellant filed an application under section 7 for initiation of CIRP against respondent - NCLT by impugned order dismissed said application on ground that amounts advanced by appellant to respondent were not financial debts as amounts advanced did not involve a time value of money - It was noted that two loan agreements clearly specified that loans were interest bearing and interest rate, time period of loans had also been specified - Whether loan agreements clearly showed that amounts advanced by appellant to respondent were in nature of financial debts, which carried time value of money - Held, yes - Whether thus, NCLT erred grossly by not considering two loan agreements and features therein were in fact relating to financial debts, which were due and payable to appellant by respondent - Held, yes [Paras 15 and 23]

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process - Financial debt - Corporate debtor availed financial assistance from applicant but committed default in repayment - Thus, applicant filed instant application under section 7 - Corporate debtor raised objections that applicant was neither a financial creditor nor debts claimed by applicant came within purview of financial debt - It also raised a dispute that amount was due and payable at convenience of corporate debtor within a period of seven years and not on demand by applicant - As regard to first objection, it was noted that loan was disbursed against consideration for time value of money with a clear commercial effect of borrowing, thus, not only present claim came within purview of financial debt but also applicant was a financial creditor - As regard to second objection, it was noted that corporate debtor had sent an email to financial creditor in which it had not only accepted its liability but also sought time to repay debt at earliest, therefore, contention of corporate debtor that amount was payable after seven years was baseless and same could not be sustained - Whether since applicant had placed on record documents to prove default in repayment and, moreover, application of applicant was complete and there was no disciplinary proceeding pending against proposed RP, said application was to be admitted - Held, yes [Paras 14, 25, 39 and 40]

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Corporate debtor availed a cash loan from financial creditor /applicant - Corporate debtor failed to repay said loan and thus, applicant filed instant petition under section 7 - In order to prove financial debt, applicant produced copy of promissory note signed by Director of corporate debtor - On perusal of promissory note, it was found that it did not contain any terms regarding repayment of amount with interest and said promissory note was not duly stamped - Whether promissory note comes under purview of section 2(22) of Indian Stamp Act and same was liable to stamp duty - Held, yes - Whether since there were no terms stipulated in promissory note that corporate debtor was liable to repay amount with interest, said promissory note could not acquire status of financial debt and same could not be considered to be disbursed against consideration for time value of money - Held, yes - Whether therefore, instant petition was to be rejected - Held, yes [Paras 30 and 35]

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant bank had sanctioned and disbursed loan amount recoverable with applicable interest by entering into loan agreements with corporate debtor - Corporate debtor had committed default in repayment of outstanding huge debt to applicant-financial creditor - Applicant-bank filed petition under section 7 for initiation of Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process against respondent-corporate debtor - Whether since loan was disbursed against consideration of time value of money with a clear commercial effect of borrowing and debt included both outstanding principal and interest, claim of debt would come within purview of financial debt and applicant bank could be termed as 'Financial Creditor' so as to prefer application under section 7 - Held, yes - Whether since applicant 'financial creditor' had placed on record voluminous and overwhelming evidence in support of claim as well as to prove default and application was complete, application filed under section 7 was to be admitted - Held, yes [Paras 51, 58, 60, 61 and 62]IBC: Where applicant bank had sanctioned and disbursed loan amounts recoverable with applicable interest by entering into loan agreements with corporate debtor but corporate debtor had defaulted in repayment of loan amount, loan being disbursed against consideration of time value of money with a clear commercial effect of borrowing would come within purview of financial debt and applicant bank was financial creditor whose application under section 7 was to be admitted

Section 238A, read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Limitation period - Petitioner provided loan to respondent in 2007 and 2008 - Understanding between petitioner and respondent did not provide a time limit for repayment of debt - Whether in absence of any contract between parties, amount needed to be repaid within three years from date when loan was advanced; thus, loan amount advanced by cheque dated 15-12-2007, 11-2-2008 and 26-3-2008 would have become due and payable on or before 14-12-2010, 10-2-2011 and 25-3-2011, respectively - Held, yes - Whether since there was no material to show that respondent made any admission of debt within such period or even subsequent thereto, instant CIRP application for non-payment filed in 2018 was grossly time barred and, hence, not maintainable - Held, yes [Para 19]

Section 5(8) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether for any creditor to become financial creditor under section 5(7), there must be a financial debt which is owed to that person and such a person can either be principal creditor to whom financial debt is owed or may be a legal assignee to whom such debt has been transferred - Held, yes - Corporate debtor was a wholly owned subsidiary of IIL - Corporate debtor had approached IIL for financial assistance, which was provided - Meanwhile, liquidation proceedings commenced against IIL and liquidator published Process Memorandum, wherein amount defaulted by corporate debtor was recorded as Rs. 5.10 crores - Appellant-financial creditor had bid for assets/receivables of IIL and entered into a Deed of Assignment with Liquidator of IIL whereby assets of IIL were transferred in favour of financial creditor - Subsequently, financial creditor issued a legal notice and filed a section 7 application against corporate debtor before NCLT, which was rejected by NCLT on ground that debt and default did not exist - It was noted that Deed of Assignment showed that 'receivables' of IIL were assigned a sum of Rs. 25 lakh only on an 'as is where is', 'as is what is' and 'whatever there is' and 'no recourse' basis and Annual Report of IIL for financial year 2015-16 had shown sum given to corporate debtor under Head of 'Receivables' and not under Head of 'Intercorporate Loan', which should have been treatment, if amount was a loan - Whether since assigned amount had been clearly shown as trade receivable in Deed of Assignment, it could not be viewed as a loan particularly when there was no contract/agreement between corporate debtor and IIL recording advance of any loan - Held, yes - Whether there was nothing placed on record by appellant to substantiate that disbursement had been made for consideration for time value of money and, thus, NCLT did not commit any error in rejecting section 7 application filed by appellant - Held, yes [Paras 14, 25 and 26]IBC : Where appellant-financial creditor filed a section 7 application against corporate debtor on basis of a Deed of Assignment, where sum given to corporate debtor by IIL was transferred to appellant, however, said sum was clearly shown as a trade receivable rather than a loan and there was no contract or agreement between corporate debtor and IIL designating sum given as a loan, NCLT did not commit any error in rejecting section 7 application filed by appellant against corporate debtor

Section 5(8), read with section  7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant-financial creditor claimed that it had advanced loan to respondent-corporate debtor - As respondent failed to repay loan, application was filed under section 7 against corporate debtor - It was noted that there was no loan agreement on record and no Board Resolution was placed or produced by applicant company empowering it to grant loan to corporate debtor and only document on strength of which applicant was claiming that debt had arisen out of loan transactions was Form 26AS reflecting credit of interest amount and deduction of TDS - Whether in absence of any loan agreement and relevant Board Resolution, merely on basis of Form 26AS, it could not be presumed that any loan was disbursed by applicant to corporate debtor, which could be treated as the financial debt - Held, yes - Whether since applicant/financial creditor had failed to demonstrate that debt claimed in its application was arising out of any loan transactions and was a financial debt, application under section 7 was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 28 and 33]

Section 5(8), read with sections 3(12) and 5(7), of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Appellant had given unsecured loan facility to respondent-corporate debtor - Corporate debtor had been paying interest on unsecured loan and also had been deducting and depositing Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) on interest paid to appellant - Corporate debtor defaulted in payment of unsecured loan - Appellant issued demand notice to corporate debtor seeking repayment of unpaid financial debt - Appellant filed application under section 7 for initiation of CIRP against corporate debtor - NCLT by impugned order rejected said application holding that appellant had failed to establish that unsecured loan he had granted fell within scope of financial debt in absence of any loan agreement setting out terms and conditions of agreement - Whether there were no documents/records to prove that appellant was financial creditor - Held, yes - Whether audited balance sheet also did not prove existence of financial debt and default as defined under section 3(12) - Held, yes - Whether since there was no financial debt and default as proved by appellant, NCLT had rightly rejected application filed by appellant under section 7 - Held, yes [Paras 16 and 17]IBC : Where appellant - financial creditor had given unsecured loan to corporate debtor but failed to prove existence of financial debt and default, NCLT had rightly rejected application filed by appellant under section 7 for initiation of CIRP against corporate debtor

Section 5(8), read with section  7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant signed a MoU, with respondent for assessing possibilities of a joint venture in field of designing, manufacturing of automobiles, automobile parts and different types of vehicles - Due to immediate requirement of funds of respondent, applicant agreed to provide financial assistance which was to be refunded at interest of 18 per cent within 30 days when transaction did not conclude - Subsequently, applicant realised that joint venture would not be possible - Applicant, thus, issued demand notice for repayment of amount of loan - Since respondent did not repay amount in question, instant application was filed under section 7 - Respondent did not raise any dispute in respect of amount payable - Whether, on facts, there existed a financial debt which respondent failed to discharge and, thus, instant application was to be admitted - Held, yes [Paras 12 and 13]

Section 5(7), read with sections 7 and 5(8), of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Financial creditor - Whether in order to maintain application filed under section 7 for initiation of corporate insolvency resolution process in respect of corporate debtor, applicant has to satisfy that applicant comes within definition of 'financial creditor' - Held, yes - Whether 'financial debt' is a debt along with interest, if any which is disbursed against consideration for time value of money - Held, yes - Applicant filed application under section 7 stating that it had entered into an arrangement of job work with respondent corporate debtor and had extended financial assistance from time-to-time to respondent-company - Whether except bald statement that it had extended huge financial assistance from time-to-time, no detailed particulars had been furnished as to when, how much amount and for what count loan was tendered - Held, yes - Whether applicant had miserably failed to furnish details of various disbursements alleged to have been made and also failed to establish that such disbursements were made for time value of money, so as to come within purview of 'financial creditor' in order to maintain application preferred under section 7 and, therefore, application was to be rejected - Held, yes [Paras 12, 15, 16, 18  19]IBC: Where applicant failed to furnish details of alleged disbursements made to corporate debtor and also failed to establish that same were made for time value of money, applicant did not come within purview of financial creditor and, therefore, petition filed under section 7 was to be dismissed

SECTION 5 OF THE INCOME-TAX ACT, 1961-INCOME-ACCRUAL OF-ASSESSEE-
COMPANY DID NOT CHARGE ANY INTEREST ON LOAN GIVEN TO ITS 
SISTER CONCERNS AND ALSO DID NOT DEBIT INTEREST TO THEIR ACCOUNTS ON GROUND THAT THEIR FINANCIAL POSITION WAS BAD-WHETHER EVEN 
THOUGH ASSESSEE FOLLOWED MERCANTILE SYSTEM OF ACCOUNTING IMPUGNED INTEREST COULD NOT BE ADDED IN ASSESSEE’S INCOME-HELD, YES

Section  7  of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, read with Section  18  of the Limitation Act, 1963 -  Corporate insolvency resolution process  -  Initiation by financial creditor  - Applicant-NBFC disbursed five ICDs to corporate debtor in May-August 2019 with due dates falling on 19.08.2019 (1st tranche), 31.08.2019 (5th tranche), 01.10.2019 (2nd tranche), 09.10.2019 (3rd tranche), and 10.10.2019 (4th tranche) - Corporate debtor did not repay on respective due dates - Applicant sought confirmations and demanded repayment by email - Corporate debtor, by email dated 19.06.2020, confirmed outstanding balance; again on 31.08.2021, it confirmed outstanding and stated that TDS on interest had been deposited; and on 18.06.2022, it acknowledged debt and committed to repay - Applicant filed section 7 application on 06.06.2025 - Whether thus, application filed on 06.06.2025 was within limitation by virtue of acknowledgments under Section 18 of Limitation Act, 1963 - Held, yes [Paras 7.12 and 7.14]

Section 28(i),  read with section 147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Business income - Chargeable as (Interest) - Assessment year 2003-04 - For relevant year, Assessing Officer initiated reassessment proceedings on ground that assessee had not offered interest income to tax in respect of loan given to Gujarat State Investment Limited (GSIL) - Tribunal noted that assessee had not received interest on such a loan for a long time because there was no interest stipulation in loan document - Tribunal further found that during assessment year in question, issue was referred for arbitration and thereupon Board of Directors of assessee-company passed a resolution not to offer interest income to tax in view of uncertainty in its receipt itself - Tribunal thus taking a view that assessee was justified in not accounting for such interest in return, set aside reassessment proceedings - Whether findings recorded by Tribunal being findings of fact, no substantial question of law arose therefrom - Held, yes [para 5] [In favour of assessee]IT: Where AO initiated reassessment proceedings on ground that assessee had not offered interest income to tax in respect of loan given to 'GSIL', in view of fact that there was no interest stipulation in loan document and, moreover, issue had been referred for arbitration and thereupon Board of Directors of assessee-company, had passed a resolution not to offer interest income to tax in view of uncertainty in its receipt itself, impugned reassessment proceedings deserved to be quashed

I. Section 5(8), read with section  7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether amount paid towards purchase of equity in corporate debtor does not constitute a financial debt - Held, yes - Appellant, financial creditor, was one of directors of respondent-corporate debtor - He claimed to have raised loan from a financial institution in his personal name and transferred same to corporate debtor for business purpose - Corporate debtor, however failed to repay loan and interest thereon to appellant - Corporate debtor however submitted that there had been misappropriation of funds from company by appellant and that two criminal complaints were filed against appellant and his accomplices with respect to various crimes committed by them against company - Whether there was nothing on record to show if any decision was taken in Board or Resolution passed to raise above alleged loans - Held, yes - Whether, since there was nothing to show that these amounts were given to corporate debtor by financial creditor, which could be termed as 'disbursement of an amount for time value for money', alleged amount could not be termed as 'financial debt' - Held, yes [Paras 15  16]IBC: Where financial creditor, ex-director of corporate debtor, claimed to have advanced loan to corporate debtor since there was nothing on record to show if any decision was taken in Board or Resolution passed to raise above alleged loans from financial creditor, alleged debt could not be termed as 'financial debt'   IBC: Where appellant's claim, debt and default related to financial year 2012-13 onwards, application under section 7 filed on 25-10-2017 was barred by limitation

Section 5(6), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, and rule 4 of the I  B (Application to Adjudicating Authority) Rules, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Dispute - Corporate debtor availed loan from financial creditor - Corporate debtor defaulted in making payment towards interest - In response to demand notice, corporate debtor raised objection that debt claimed was not disbursed against consideration for time value of money - Corporate debtor also claimed that loan agreement relied upon by financial creditor was false and fabricated for purpose of filing instant application - Corporate debtor had placed on record reports of two experts in support of contention that alleged loan agreement was forged - It was noted that stamp paper on which loan agreement was prepared was purchased 9 days after corporate debtor was incorporated - Further, FIR had been lodged against financial creditor for having forged said alleged loan agreement - Whether facts of case created doubt on genuineness of loan agreement and therefore, matter required proper trial and investigation - Held, yes - Whether thus, instant application filed by financial creditor to initiate CIRP against corporate debtor was to be dismissed as not maintainable - Held, yes [Paras 46  47]IBC: Where financial creditor filed application under section 7 alleging that corporate debtor defaulted in payment of interest amount, since, loan agreement relied upon by financial creditor was seriously disputed, matter required proper trial and investigation and, thus, instant application was to be dismissed

Section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Initiation by financial creditor - Appellant/financial creditor, through multiple financial facilities advanced financial debt to Tajikistani company, which was a subsidiary of corporate debtor - Said financial facilities were duly guaranteed by corporate debtor - When principal borrower failed to repay outstanding interest, financial creditor recalled said facilities - Corporate guarantee issued by corporate debtor had also been invoked - Later on, financial creditor filed instant application for initiating CIRP against corporate debtor - It was a case of corporate debtor that at time of recall of loan, obligations under loan agreement were under suspension by orders of Economic Court at Tajikistan - Therefore, there could not be invocation of guarantee by corporate debtor - Further, despite representations made by principal borrower, no reconciliation of accounts had been done by financial creditor in terms of final judgment of Economic Court and in absence of reconciliation, no demand had been made by financial creditor upon principal borrower to pay amount of recalculated interest - Whether corporate guarantee given by corporate debtor could be invoked only in event of a default on part of principal borrower - Held, yes - Whether since, in instant case, there was no fresh demand made by financial creditor to principal borrower for recalculated interest, there was no debt that was due and/or payable and, therefore, there was no default by principal borrower for recalculated interest - Held, yes - Whether thus, application to initiate CIRP against corporate debtor was to be rejected - Held, yes [Para 24]IBC: Where financial creditor advanced loan to a Tajikistani company, which was subsidiary of corporate guarantor and obligations under loan agreement were under suspension by orders of Economic Court at Tajikistan, since in terms of final judgment of Economic Court, no fresh demand had been made upon principal borrower to pay recalculated interest, there could not be assumption of default by principal borrower

Section 5(8), read with sections 5(7) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant bank filed application under section 7 to initiate corporate insolvency resolution process against respondent corporate debtor claiming that a sum was due from respondent company along with pendentelite interest - Whether since loan was disbursed by applicant against consideration for time value of money with a clear commercial effect of borrowing and debt claimed included both component of outstanding principal and interest, applicant's claim came within purview of 'financial debt' - Held, yes - Whether since applicant-financial creditor was entitled to claim its outstanding financial debt from corporate debtor and there had been default in payment of financial debt, application filed under section 7 was to be admitted and moratorium was to be declared - Held, yes [Paras 39, 47, 50, 51 and 54]IBC : Where applicant had disbursed loan to corporate debtor against consideration for time value of money with a clear commercial effect of borrowing, debt came within purview of financial debt and applicant-financial debtor was entitled to claim its outstanding financial debt from corporate debtor when there was default in payment

Section 5(8), read with  sections 5(7) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether 'Financial debt' means outstanding principal due in respect of a loan and would also include interest thereon, if any interest were payable thereon; if there is no interest payable on loan, only outstanding principal would qualify as a financial debt - Held, yes - Whether trigger for initiation of Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process by a financial creditor under section 7 is occurrence of a default by corporate debtor - Held, yes - Whether definition of 'Financial Debt' in section 5(8) does not expressly exclude an interest free loan - Held, yes - Whether 'Financial Debt' would have to be construed to include interest free loans advanced to finance business operations of a corporate body - Held, yes - Whether thus, a person who gives a term loan to a corporate person, free of interest, on account of its working capital requirements is a financial creditor, and, therefore, is competent to initiate corporate resolution process under section 7 - Held, yes [Paras 22 and 31]IBC : Definition of 'Financial Debt' in section 5(8) does not expressly exclude an interest free loan; a person who gives a term loan to a corporate person free of interest on account of its working capital requirements is a financial creditor, and, therefore, is competent to initiate Corporate Insolvency resolution process under section 7

facts.text:
■

The applicant- financial creditor claimed that it had extended a loan to the Corporate Debtor during the period from 13.06.2007 to 27.03.2009. The said loan was extended in his personal capacity and was repayable on demand.

■

Corporate Debtor had consistently acknowledged the said loan in its Audited Financial Statements over the years, classifying it as an “Unsecured Loan”.

■

A loan recall notice was issued by the financial creditor on 04.07.2022 demanding immediate repayment of the full outstanding loan. A reminder for payment was further issued via email on 01.08.2022. In response to the aforementioned notice, the Corporate Debtor, through its Financial Controller acknowledged the communication and expressed an intention to amicably settle the matter. Since no steps were taken by the Corporate Debtor to repay the debt a legal notice was issued by the financial creditor.

■

Thus, financial creditor filed instant petition under section 7 to initiate CIRP against corporate debtor for the alleged default on the part of the corporate debtor in repayment of financial debt.

■

The Corporate Debtor raised a dispute that the application under Section 7 was barred by limitation, as the alleged financial debt was stated to have arisen in the year 2005-06, and the demand was purportedly made for the first time in July 2022- after a lapse of nearly 17 years. The corporate debtor argued that such a stale claim could not be revived by unilateral recall or reliance upon self-serving accounting entries. Further, it was contended that the application failed to satisfy the statutory preconditions of Section 7.

■

The corporate debtor also claimed that financial creditor had failed to produce any loan agreement, repayment schedule, or even a basic acknowledgment of terms such as interest, tenure, or security. No board resolution or authorization was passed by corporate debtor to borrow funds from the financial creditor. The absence of any documentation, along with the lack of demand for repayment for nearly two decades, was said to indicate that the financial creditor never extended any loan capable of forming a financial debt.

The respondents-financial creditors extended a financial facility of Rs. 3.10 crores to the corporate debtor, out of which the corporate debtor returned an amount of Rs. 15 lacs to the respondents.

A demand notice was issued to the corporate debtor by the respondents demanding repayment of an unpaid loan in default with interest.

In reply, to demand notice, the corporate debtor, vide letter alleged that loan was given for tenure of 5 years, hence, the notice had been issued mala fidely by respondent and requested for withdrawal of said notice.

The respondents again sent notice to the corporate debtor for repayment of the amount, including principal as well as interest, and filed an application under section 7 against the corporate debtor.

The NCLT, by an impugned order, admitted said application.

On appeal, the appellant suspended director of the corporate debtor submitted that there was no loan agreement entered into between the corporate debtor and there was no financial debt.

The appellant further submitted that the respondents were not registered under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, and respondents had no license and, therefore, could not have extended any loan to the corporate debtor.

The petitioner-financial creditor had provided an unsecured loan of Rs. 1.11 crores to the respondent-corporate debtor on 9-1-2007.

The petitioner had issued a demand notice dated 14-9-2017. In reply to said notice, the corporate debtor submitted that the payment of Rs. 1.11 crores was not towards 25 per cent equity interest but was rather an investment in a development project of a corporate debtor.

On default in making payment, the petitioner had filed an application under section 7 to initiate CIRP against the corporate debtor.

The respondent submitted that petitioner had advanced an unsecured loan to the respondent on 9-1-2007 however, petition filed by the appellant in 2020 i.e., after a lapse of 13 years further, petitioner through letter dated 14-9-2017 himself had claimed that the amount was paid for acquisition of 25 per cent equity interest in the development project of the corporate debtor.

■

The appellant was a financial creditor of the corporate debtor(CD). The appellant had advanced an interest free loan to the corporate debtor to discharge the liabilities of the other secured financial creditors. The loan advanced by the appellant did not bear interest and was to be repaid after the settlement of the secured financial loans of the CD under the one time settlement scheme but when the CD failed to repay the loan after settlement of the secured loans, the appellant issued notice and recalled its loan to be repaid within 15 days. The appellant alleged that the amount of loan was reflected in the financial statement of the Respondent as unsecured loan. The corporate debtor failed to repay the loan after settlement of the secured loans.

■

The appellant filed an application under section 7 for the resolution of an interest free loan. The NCLT dismissed the application on ground that amount given by the appellant to the corporate debtor was not a financial debt and, hence, the corporate debtor was not owed to pay the appellant and that the loan was advanced in violation of section 186(2) of the Companies Act, 2013 and, therefore, was void and unforceable.

■

On appeal:

The assessee-firm showed certain borrowings on 2-1-1963 in its books. The loan was shown to have been taken from R against four pronotes. This loan was shown to have been returned on 19-7-1965. The assessee filed confirmation letter from the aforesaid creditor. In a statement and cross-examination, the creditor affirmed that the money transactions with the assessee were not of a genuine nature, that he had never advanced any money to the assessee nor received back any money from the assessee and that the transaction was a mere Havala or accommodation entry in which no money had passed whatsoever. As the assessment involved an addition of more than Rs. 1 lakh, the Assessing Officer referred the matter to the IAC. The IAC, on the basis of the aforesaid facts, held that there was no bona fide transaction between the assessee and the alleged lender. On the basis of the directions of the IAC under section 144B the ITO added back the aforesaid cash credit and also disallowed the interest claim on the aforesaid loan. On appeal, the Commissioner (Appeals) upheld the aforesaid addition.

On second appeal:

The corporate debtor was a family company that struggled financially and was indebted to various banks/financial institutions and there was no access to funds.

On request of other directors and to bail out the corporate debtor, the respondent No.-1 financial creditor, had lent a sum of Rs. 9.15 crores from time to time as financial loans.

The financial creditor also issued a loan of Rs. 13.84 crores and was entitled to interest at 14 per cent per annum.

Thereafter, the corporate debtor, was requested by financial creditor, to return amount, without any success, a letter dated 17-11-2021 was issued to corporate debtor in which it was stated that he had infused funds, into the company, for the past few years, and those monies were brought in as unsecured loans, to save the company, from its repayment obligations.

However, no reply was received from the corporate debtor, on default in making payment, the petition under section 7 was filed by the financial creditor against the corporate debtor.

The corporate debtor alleged that the financial debt of Rs. 13.84 crores without any basis and, it was the duty of the financial creditor to annex all material documents along with the Form I in order to substantiate its debt.

The corporate debtor further alleged that section 7 casts an obligation on the financial creditor to furnish the record of default and, the corporate debtor had three shareholders, who were also directors of the corporate debtor and, thus it was not out of place to state that the said shareholder directors were own brothers.

The NCLT admitted said petition under section 7 and, declared moratorium under section 14.

The appellant, shareholders and suspended director of the corporate debtor filed instant appeal on ground that impugned order passed by NCLT in admitting the section 7 application was per se an illegal and an invalid one, because of the fact that there was no privity of contract, between the corporate debtor and the financial creditor appellant. The appellant further alleged that there was no agreement or document, proving loan, was taken by the corporate debtor, from the financial creditor.

The respondent corporate debtor availed a loan/inter corporate deposit from the applicant/financial creditor vide loan agreement.

As per the loan agreement executed between the parties, the loan was to be repaid with interest. In terms of agreement the interest was to become payable from the beginning of financial year following the moratorium period or upon demand by financial creditor whichever was later, the determination of which was to be at the sole option of financial creditor.

Thereafter, the financial creditor vide various communications requested the corporate debtor to repay the loan amount but the corporate debtor failed to repay the same. Thus, the financial creditor was constrained to issue a demand notice but the corporate debtor maliciously denied such admitted amount as due and payable to the financial creditor.

The corporate debtor in its reply had raised objection that the debt claimed in the petition was not disbursed against interest or consideration for time value of money and therefore the claim of the applicant was not a financial debt. It was contended that no interest or time period for repayment was ever prescribed on the alleged transaction.

Corporate debtor had also alleged that the sole loan agreement relied upon by the financial creditor was false and fabricated for the purpose of filing of the present application. It was claimed that apart from the alleged forged loan document, there was nothing on record to show that the corporate debtor ever agreed to pay any such interest component.

Accordingly, it was argued that the applicant was not a 'financial creditor' and the debt claimed in the application did not come within the purview of 'financial debt' and therefore the present application was not maintainable.
